claims: EASA is the EU's authority for aviation safety.
EASA is headquartered in Cologne, Germany.
EASA manages the "EU air safety list" of banned operators.
EASA updates Conflict Zone Information Bulletins (CZIB) for risk assessment.
EASA is an agency of the European Commission.
EASA has a Management Board representing EU Member States.
EASA's budget is partly funded by the EU.
EASA's budget is partly funded through industry certification fees.
EASA has a satellite office in Brussels.
There is another entity known as "EASA" called The Electro•Mechanical Authority.
The Electro•Mechanical Authority is a separate organization for the electrical repair industry.
